note:
Independent read-only review of REHEARSAL_CLEANUP_20261012. Verified TASK_EN.md, manifest.json, remote-provenance.json, dry-run.json, cleanup-reviewed.sh, and all four cited production-checkpoint.json files (ACTOR_RELEASE_20261012, SINGER_RELEASE_20261012, CULTURE_VARIETY_RELEASE_20261012, CULTURE_NEXT2_20261012). Findings: (1) The 8 targets are exactly actors-3556b59 x2, singers-1c9b534 x2, culture-variety-b015251 x2, culture-7d7a163(next2) x2, matching task scope; protected_builds correctly excludes the current reader build (4207ef5) and culture-next4 (c15eefc), consistent with recent git log. (2) All four checkpoint files show ACCEPTED static+execution reviews with migration/integrity/old_api_rollback PASS and old_rows_preserved true, corroborating the manifest's per-rehearsal provenance results (same PASS/true pattern, independent data points from production builds vs rehearsal DB counts). (3) Script containment: hostname pin, flock on DEPLOY.lock, kubectl image-digest and PVC-UID pinning before any Python runs. (4) Python guards: root and each target path required to equal their own os.path.resolve() (rejects any symlink in the chain, including root itself); parent/build-dir relationship checked structurally (parent.parent==root, parent.name==build); build must not be in protected_builds; exact file-set equality check {api.log, quiz.sqlite, rollback-api} with no extra/symlinked members; rehearsal result/script files re-hashed against remote-provenance.json sha256 values (ties deletion eligibility to the exact reviewed rehearsal evidence, not just manifest text); rehearsal result JSON is independently re-parsed and re-checked (migration/integrity/old_rows_preserved/old_api_rollback) rather than trusted from manifest. (5) Process-in-use guard walks /proc, checking cwd/exe/every fd of every PID for symlink targets inside any target path before deletion — covers open-file and cwd cases. (6) Deletion is exact and non-recursive: api.log is renamed to a preserved sidecar (verified not pre-existing, then re-hashed after rename), quiz.sqlite and rollback-api are unlinked by exact name (no glob/wildcard/recursive rm), then rmdir (which only succeeds on an empty dir, i.e. only if exactly those 3 known files were present) — matches 'quiz.sqlite and rollback-api unlinked, api.log preserved' requirement. No backups/archives/images/PVC are touched. dry-run.json confirms all 8 preflight guards currently pass.

Limitations I could not close in a read-only desk review: I did not SSH, execute, or re-run anything — I verified guard logic by reading source, not by observing a live run. The process-in-use /proc scan and the kubectl/hostname pins are checked only immediately before deletion inside the same script run, so there is an inherent (small) TOCTOU window between the guard check and the unlink/rmdir calls; this is a design limitation to note, not a defect given the flock and narrow execution window. I relied on the provenance file's own reported SHA256 values rather than recomputing them myself against remote bytes, since the targets live on a remote host I'm not touching. Acceptance here certifies the reviewed plan/script/evidence only, not runtime execution or a post-run production check; the four checkpoint files are themselves the lead's/other reviewers' prior evidence, not something I re-executed.

acceptance: Exact path provenance from successful checkpoints and run scripts
Containment, symlink, active process guards; preserve logs; immutable reviewed manifest
